title: NIO vs. Tesla: Which EV Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
NIO vs. Tesla: Which EV Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool

TSLA
NIO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As the transition to electric transportation accelerates, investors often weigh the rapid growth of NIO Inc. (NYSE:NIO) against the established dominance of Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) to determine which is the better buy today.

NIO focuses on the luxury segment in China and Europe, utilizing unique battery-swapping stations to address charging concerns. Conversely, Tesla leverages massive manufacturing scale and software integration to lead the global market. Comparing these two involves balancing NIO's high-speed expansion against Tesla's proven profitability and massive capital reserves.

The case for NIO

NIO designs and sells smart electric vehicles under several brands, including its namesake line and the newer ONVO and Firefly labels. It targets premium buyers across 24 countries, emphasizing a user enterprise model that integrates lifestyle services with vehicle ownership. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of its revenue, providing a diversified sales base.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $13.1 billion, an increase of approximately 33.1% from the prior year. Despite this growth, the company reported a net loss of about $2.2 billion for the period. While the net margin improved from the previous two years, it remained negative at roughly 17.1%. (Note that figures have been converted from Chinese Yuan as of the publication date).

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 6.3x, which measures total debt against the value of shareholder equity. The current ratio, which gauges the ability to cover short-term obligations with current assets, is roughly 1.0x. Free cash flow, or cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was negative $461.2 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 59.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Tesla

Tesla operates as a vertically integrated manufacturer of electric vehicles and energy storage systems, selling directly to consumers without a traditional dealership network. It serves a diverse group of residential and utility-scale customers, while partnering with firms like Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (OTC:CYATY) for battery cells. This strategy allows the company to capture value across the entire energy ecosystem.

For FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $94.8 billion, a decrease of nearly 2.9% year over year. The company recorded net income of roughly $3.8 billion, resulting in a net margin of close to 4%. This represents a decline from the double-digit net margins seen in previous fiscal years.

title: Fund Manager Lists Three Reasons He Still Won’t Buy Tesla Stock

Fund Manager Lists Three Reasons He Still Won’t Buy Tesla Stock
Anan Ashraf

AAPL

Black said Tesla has underinvested in both marketing talent and spending, keeping it from breaching Apple's market valuation.

He also argued that Tesla has not leveraged its brand into marketable categories such as conventional pickups and compact vehicles priced under $30,000.

On valuation, Black pointed to Tesla's 2027 price-to-earnings multiple of 173 times, which he called extreme.

Gary Black, managing partner of The Future Fund LLC, on Tuesday outlined three reasons he still does not own Tesla Inc. (TSLA) shares despite "great technological progress on FSD and Robotaxi," including valuation concerns and lack of marketing investment.

Black said he sold his firm's Tesla position in May 2025 at $356. Since then, the stock has risen only about 5% while the S&P 500 has gained 24% and the Nasdaq has gained 26%, he wrote on Tuesday while detailing his three reasons for not stepping back in.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Reason 1: Lack Of Marketing Investment

Black said Tesla has underinvested in both marketing talent and spending. "In talking with former TSLA executives, my sense is that Elon Musk's marketing strategy is to rely on word-of-mouth to sell $TSLA products, which is not scalable," he wrote.

"TSLA is appropriately run by engineers but to approach $AAPL's $5 trillion valuation, TSLA needs to learn how to communicate product benefits with mainstream consumers and not just the engineering types who already own TSLA products," he wrote.

Reason 2: Failure To Extend The Brand

Black argued that Tesla has not leveraged its brand into marketable categories such as conventional pickups and compact vehicles priced under $30,000. He noted that the company spent years promoting the Cybertruck, priced near $100,000 for its more premium variants, which "was not accepted by mainstream truck owners," instead of developing a conventional-looking electric pickup under $40,000 that might have gained more customer interest.

He estimated that a conventional truck priced around $45,000 that captured just 3% of the global pickup market, which he put at roughly 8% of total vehicle sales, could have generated $1.5 billion in net income and roughly $250 billion in additional market value. The sub-$30,000 compact segment represents another large missed opportunity, he said.

Reason 3: Valuation Concerns

On valuation, Black pointed to Tesla's 2027 price-to-earnings multiple of 173 times, which he called extreme relative to his firm's forecast of roughly 45% annual earnings growth over the next five years.

title: Tesla Plans $3.3 Billion German Factory Expansion for Cybercab Production
detail:
Tesla Plans $3.3 Billion German Factory Expansion for Cybercab Production
Faizan Farooque
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:57 PM CST 1 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA, Financials) revealed plans to invest some $3.3 billion in its German manufacturing plant as the company ramps up capacity for future Cybercab production.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

TSLA GF Value chart

The investment will fund another production hall at Tesla's plant in Gruenheide near Berlin, its only vehicle production site in Europe.

The expanded site is planned to produce as many as 1 million Cybercab robotaxis per year, Tesla said.

The company expects to submit its building permit application by the end of 2026.

Construction is expected to start in the first half of 2027, with Cybercab production starting in 2029.

Gruenheide could become the biggest car-making hub in Germany by production capacity, possibly outranking Volkswagens Wolfsburg plant.

Tesla also anticipates generating additional jobs, initially looking for several hundred workers for construction and production planning.

The announcement comes as several German automakers are struggling with weaker demand, rising manufacturing costs and competition from Chinese vehicle manufacturers.

Yet Teslas plans are risky.

The Cybercab has not yet been sold in large numbers, and the demand for the vehicle is unclear.

Tesla has also encountered environmental protests and labor disputes at its German factory.

The company recently ramped up Model Y production at Gruenheide and plans to start battery cell production there in 2027.

For investors, the expansion represents a big bet on Tesla's autonomous vehicle strategy.

Next steps include regulatory approval for the new facility and likely construction to start in 2027.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares decreased 0.51% to $377.81 at 10:45 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles published a new automated vehicle report showing Tesla's driverless fleet nearly level with Waymo's in the state. Tesla Robotaxi LLC had 1,306 vehicles authorized as of November 16, against 1,321 for Waymo.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

TSLA GF Value chart

Tesla added 226 authorizations in the 18 days since the October 29 report, a 21% jump, while Waymo added 62, or about 5%, according to GoodCarBadCar's analysis of the state data. Texas now lists 3,451 authorized vehicles across 17 companies, more than double the 1,457 reported in June. JPMorgan reiterated a Neutral rating and $430 price target on November 16, citing cumulative unsupervised mileage of about 5.3 million, up from roughly 1.4 million at the end of the third quarter.

Authorizations are permission slips, not paid rides, and JPMorgan estimates only about 700 Tesla vehicles are active nationally. At the recent pace, though, Tesla would pass Waymo's Texas count within days. GuruFocus gives Tesla a GF Score of 86/100, backed by a strong balance sheet but held back by thin profitability, with net margin near 3%. Its GF Value of $359.98 leaves the shares about 5% above that mark, a fairly valued reading, so the robotaxi story is already in the price rather than ignored. The next test is whether active vehicles and paid miles grow as fast as the authorization list.

title: Musk Says Owners’ Tesla Robotaxi Trials “May Start” Next Month. That’s a Threat to Uber
detail:
Musk Says Owners’ Tesla Robotaxi Trials “May Start” Next Month. That’s a Threat to Uber
Roxanna Maglangit
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 11:35 AM CST 6 min read
TSLA
UBER
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Musk Says Owners' Tesla Robotaxi Trials "May Start" Next Month. That's a Threat to Uber ©U.S. Air Force photo and Bl∡ke from Pexels via Canva]
Key Takeaways

Elon Musk said on Monday that trials letting Tesla owners add their own cars to the Robotaxi network may start next month, if things go well.

Owners' cars would let Tesla grow its fleet without buying the cars, as it guides to about $20 billion of capital spending this year.

Each owner who sends a car out for Tesla is a car Uber loses, and Uber's operating margin only turned positive in 2023.

Musk's robotaxi dates have slipped before, so the date to watch is when owners' cars start earning money in the network. Tesla has put that around the second quarter of 2027.

An Uber driver in Austin just told Elon Musk he'd rather his Model Y work for Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) without him than keep driving it for Uber Technologies (UBER:NYSE). Musk says owners like him may get to start trying that as soon as next month.

The driver calls himself a "Diamond level Uber driver in the Austin area (using FSD exclusively)," and said in a post on X that he gets "anywhere between 49% and 63% of the passenger fare."

His conclusion: "I'd rather send my Model Y off to work for Robotaxi without me."

Musk's response on Monday? "Coming soon. If things [go] well, may start trials next month."

Then he added a pitch to every driver reading: "Much better to manage a fleet of cars than have to drive just one car by yourself!"

Trials would beat Tesla's own timeline

That's earlier than anything Tesla has said before. On its third-quarter call in October, management said customer cars would join the Robotaxi fleet "somewhere around Q2 next year." JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta expects the same timing. In a note to clients on Sunday, he wrote that customer-owned cars running unsupervised FSD should become "another, capital-light source of supply" for the network starting in the second quarter of 2027.

A trial is still short of owners actually getting paid. But trials next month would start testing the Model Ys already in owners' garages months ahead of that date. The news also comes days after Tesla began inviting select customers to buy a Cybercab. Those cars are for personal use only, and Tesla hasn't said whether they'll ever be able to join the network.

Analysts aren't counting on owners' cars yet

title: Tesla commits $3.30bn to expand German gigafactory for Cybercab
detail:
Tesla commits $3.30bn to expand German gigafactory for Cybercab
Annual output of the vehicle at the facility is projected to scale up to as many as one million units. Credit: Jonathan Weiss / Shutterstock.com · Just Auto · Jonathan Weiss / Shutterstock.com
GlobalData
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 11:48 AM CST 2 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

US electric vehicle maker Tesla has committed approximately €3bn ($3.30bn) to enlarge its Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg plant situated in Grünheide, Germany.

The funding encompasses the addition of a new production hall intended for manufacturing the autonomous Cybercab starting in 2029.

Annual output of the vehicle at the facility is projected to scale up to as many as one million units.

According to Tesla, the enlargement will establish the Grünheide facility as its most technologically advanced gigafactory.

In a LinkedIn post, Andre Thierig, senior director, manufacturing at Giga Berlin, revealed that staff had been informed of the project, with building works scheduled to begin during the first half of the year.

Tesla stated that the project will also generate further employment, with initial staffing focused on building and production-planning posts.

"This announcement for expansion is, of course, also the starting signal for the creation of further new jobs! We are hiring immediately, primarily in the areas of construction and production planning!" Thierig said.

Brandenburg Minister-President Dietmar Woidke welcomed the investment announcement in a statement.

He said: "This is a great day for Brandenburg and a strong signal for Germany as an industrial location. The investment of three billion euros and the prospect of producing up to one million Cybercabs in Grünheide in the future is a decision of enormous economic importance. Tesla is once again placing its trust in Brandenburg, in our location, and above all in the capabilities of our employees."

The development follows an announcement made by Tesla earlier this month detailing plans to taper off Cybertruck assembly at its Gigafactory Texas site midway through next year.

The move is intended to reallocate manufacturing capacity towards the autonomous Cybercab model.

Company CEO Elon Musk verified the cancellation, stating that production will wind down to accommodate greater Cybercab volumes.

The decision arrived after prolonged periods of sluggish sales, and it remains unconfirmed whether manufacturing will move to a different location or stop permanently.

The factory enlargement also follows Tesla's latest financial results, published last month, which showed that net income attributable to common stockholders declined 42.7% year-on-year to $787m in the third quarter of 2026.

"Tesla commits $3.30bn to expand German gigafactory for Cybercab" was originally created and published by Just Auto, a GlobalData owned brand.
